capex_override.ack_reason: Out-of-band by construction: the engine has no filed capex value to band against (last filed value is null under every candidate tag in all periods of companyfacts), so any value flags out-of-band. The $0 is not an estimate — it is proven by the filer's own FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement, which contains no capex line and reconciles exactly without one in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025.
capex_override.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 under every candidate tag the engine reads because, as a specialty P&C insurer, AFG reports no capital expenditures at all: its cash deployment (purchases of investments) is an investing activity for the insurance portfolio, and it carries no operating PP&E base on the balance sheet. The filing's own cash-flow reconciliation proves the capex amount is $0, not an undisclosed purchase (EG/CMPS-style proof). The engine's history already carried capex as assumed-zero, so the override changes no OE figure — it converts a silent zero-fill into a sourced, registered decision.
capex_override.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-25), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows: the investing-activities section lists only acquisitions ($7M in FY2025), purchases of investments ($2,984M), sales/maturities of investments ($2,437M) and other investing activities (-$7M) — there is no purchases-of-property-and-equipment or any capital-expenditures line for FY2025, FY2024 or FY2023, and the balance sheet carries no property-and-equipment line. The statement fully reconciles without one (this run's statements.json, filing-direct): FY2025 operating $1,533M + investing -$835M + financing -$377M = the reported net change in cash of $321M exactly; FY2024: $1,152M + $95M - $1,066M = reported $181M exactly; FY2023: $1,970M + $414M - $2,031M = reported $353M exactly. EDGAR companyfacts for CIK 1042046 contains no capex fact under any candidate tag in any period (statements.json warning: no capital-expenditure figure filed for 69 periods with operating cash flow).

moat_against: Insurance capacity is close to a commodity — no network effects and low switching costs; pricing is set by the industry cycle, which is softening
Social inflation on U.S. casualty lines and catastrophe exposure can produce reserve charges that erase underwriting profit
Earnings depend materially on investment returns, including alternative investments (7.1% annualized in Q2 2026 vs a 10%+ long-term target) — volatile and market-driven
Gross margin is not a meaningful insurer metric and the roic_proxy is an operating-income construct; the durable evidence is ROE, which is float-levered
Crop insurance seasonality concentrates profitability in Q4; workers' comp pricing was down ~2% in Q2 2026
moat_for: Diversified specialty P&C platform (~36 niche businesses) with granular underwriting expertise in hard-to-insure commercial niches
Combined ratio better than the industry average for more than two decades; 91.5% in Q2 2026
Sustained returns: roic_proxy 17.3-19.6% and ROE 17.5-20.0% in FY2023-25 (fundamentals.json)
Pricing power in the current cycle: renewal rate increases ~5% ex workers' comp for four consecutive quarters through Q2 2026
Disciplined, opportunistic capital allocation: $707M returned in FY2025 including special dividends, debt/total capital 27.5% at FY2025
moat_justification: Diversified specialty P&C franchise (~36 niche businesses via Great American) with a combined ratio better than the industry for more than two decades and sustained high returns (fundamentals.json roic_proxy 17.3-19.6% in FY2023-25, ROE 17.5-20.0%), but insurance capacity is close to a commodity: no network effects, modest switching costs, price set by the cycle, and social inflation / catastrophe / alternative-investment returns can erase a year of underwriting profit.
name: American Financial Group, Inc.
one_liner: Quality specialty P&C insurer, moat 5/10 — B by numbers (16.1% weighted IRR, IV@15% $163 vs $149 price) but the OCF base capitalizes float (TTM OCF $1,566M vs TTM net income $953M), so sized down to C per the insurer-float rule and the bear end (C) of the tier band; clears 15% only below ~$163 on these inputs.

sbc_override.reason: AFG tags SBC only in annual filings; its 10-Q cash-flow statements present no stock-compensation YTD fact, so ttm.py exits with 'sbc: no post-FY YTD fact' and no TTM base can be built (statements.json likewise warns the filings for 2025-03-31..2026-06-30 carry no SBC cash-flow line). This override lets ttm.py assemble the SBC legs at the last filed annual rate, prorated by days. SBC is ~1.2% of FY2025 OCF ($18M vs $1,533M), so the proration assumption moves TTM OE/share by cents, not dollars. The engine's annual history is unaffected: SBC is filed for every annual period, and an override never replaces a filed value.
sbc_override.source: Last filed SBC: FY2025 AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense $18,000,000 (Form 10-K FY2025; the same $18M figure is filed for FY2023 and FY2024) — the anchor named here; value is exactly 1.0x that filed figure, inside the 0.1x-10x estimate band

tier_override_reason: Insurer-float softening (Andrew's standing rule, 2026-10-15): the OCF-based owner's-earnings base capitalizes float — TTM OCF $1,566M vs TTM net income $953M (fundamentals.json), and FY2023/FY2025 show the same >40% NI/OCF divergence — so the final tier is sized down one notch from tier_by_numbers B to C, even though the TTM base ($18.63/share) sits close to the normalized median ($18.14/share). This also lands on the bear end of the TIER_BAND (bear C 11.6% vs bull B 19.5%), per the 5.4 sizing rule. Same treatment as PFG/EG/AIZ/ACGL/HIG/WRB.
